newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-GREAT BRITAIN SEEKS SUPER LEAGUE TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-GREAT BRITAIN SEEKS SUPER LEAGUE TEST.

text.p: Britain wants to play a rugby
league international against Rupert Murdoch's Australian Super
League side later this month, English Rugby League chairman
Maurice Lindsay said on Friday.
Reacting to a court ruling freeing media baron Murdoch to
launch Super League in Australia next year, Lindsay said he
wanted to add the match to Britain's current South Pacific tour.
"We will almost certainly have an international between
Australia and Great Britain during the current Great Britain
tour (of the South Pacific)," Lindsay said from London in an
interview on Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio.
"We are going to sit down after this very interview...and
discuss the matter with our Australian colleagues and try and
find a venue and a date in October to have an inaugural game
between Great Britain and Australia Super League," he said.
Britain, who joined the Murdoch camp in April last year, are
due to play Super League allies Fiji on Saturday.
Murdoch on Friday said his rebel Super League would kick off
in Australia in 1997 after a court ruled that attempts to stop
the rebel competition violated anti-monopoly laws.
The Federal Court of Australia upheld Murdoch's appeal
against an earlier court ruling in favour of the sport's
national body, the Australian Rugby League (ARL).
The original ruling banned Super League from kicking off in
Australia in competition against the existing ARL premiership
before the year 2000, forcing Murdoch to shelve plans to launch
a 10-team competition this year.
